judged_text: The third argument passed to refreshOAuthTokens is credentialId (the credential row id) where the parameter is userId and every other call site in the diff passes credential.userId. The sync request carries calcomUserId=<credential id>, so the parent endpoint resolves the wrong (or no) user and can return another user's tokens into this credential row; team credentials also take the sync path because credentialId is always truthy, where every other app falls back to local refresh for them.

The sync request carries calcomUserId=<credential id>, so the parent endpoint resolves the wrong (or no) user and can return another user's tokens into this credential row; team credentials also take the sync path because credentialId is always truthy, where every other app falls back to local refresh for them.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the call `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` passes `credentialId` as the third argument, while `refreshOAuthTokens`’s third parameter is explicitly `userId: number | null` (see `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`). Every other modified call site in the diff passes `credential.userId`. If `credentialId` is the credential row id (as its name suggests), the sync request will send `calcomUserId=<credential id>` instead of the Cal.com user id, and it will also bypass the intended `userId`-null guard for non-user/team credentials.
